- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day peaks); apply smoothing filter or cap forecast at 2x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is below 1.5, forecast should not exceed 1.8 unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to overshoot; apply downward correction on 3rd+ day of such cycle.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.67/0.00) — increase forecast by 15–20% for such periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 10x historical mean, model is likely underestimating; apply multiplicative scaling (e.g., ×1.5) if sentiment is bullish and volatility is high.
